interpretation.peak_vs_persistence: Peak Major 53/57 (93.0%) is much higher than fixed-window Major: T+10 27/54 (50.0%) and T+20 27/52 (51.9%). This shows that eventual high achievement and being in a major role at a fixed later time are different outcomes.
interpretation.apex_pattern: Lifetime peak Apex is 24/57 (42.1%), versus T+10 3/54 (5.6%) and T+20 10/52 (19.2%). The T+20 increase over T+10 reflects later-generation executives/scientists/cultural leaders reaching apex while some older leaders retire or die; it is not a cumulative survival curve.
interpretation.activity_floor: Scope >=2 remains high: T+10 50/54 (92.6%) and T+20 44/52 (84.6%), indicating broad long-run professional/public activity even when major leadership is no longer held.

guardrails: The original primary denominator remains 60 selected units; these are person-only secondary metrics.
Organization units are not missing and are reported separately under organization axes.
Deaths are competing events and excluded from assessable snapshot denominators.
Fixed-window scores do not inherit earlier lifetime peaks or former titles.
T+10 and T+20 are independent window snapshots, not cumulative success probabilities.
Field heterogeneity makes pooled person57 values descriptive rather than causal or outlet-superiority estimates.
